entry.title: Build A Reasoning Model Scratch 2: Loading a Base Model, Text Generation, and KV Caching

media:group.media:title: Build A Reasoning Model Scratch 2: Loading a Base Model, Text Generation, and KV Caching
media:group.media:description:

entry.title: OpenAI Astra and Recurrent Depth / Looped Transformers

media:group.media:title: OpenAI Astra and Recurrent Depth / Looped Transformers
media:group.media:description:
A short video explaining the rumored recurrent depth (looped transformer) architectural design in OpenAI's new (upcoming) Astra model.
In particular, I discuss what looped transformers are and go over the related literature.
Links and references
The Information article on OpenAI Astra: https://www.theinformation.com/articles/secret-technique-behind-openais-astra-model-sparks-security-concerns
Looped depth sharing explainer: https://sebastianraschka.com/llm-architecture-gallery/looped-depth-sharing/
LLM Architecture Gallery: https://www.sebastianraschka.com/llm-architecture-gallery/
Nanbeige4.2-3B technical report: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22083
Mixture-of-Recursions: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.10524
Universal Transformers: https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.03819
Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05171
00:00 OpenAI Astra and the Recurrent-Depth Rumor 01:37 Claims About Recurrent Depth 03:02 Nanbeige4.2-3B’s Looped Transformer 05:21 Why Reuse the Same Layers? 07:43 Training From Scratch vs. Retrofitting 09:47 Why Use Two Passes? 10:35 KV-Cache Implications 12:00 Mixture-of-Recursions and Dynamic Depth 16:18 Validation-Loss Comparison 18:16 Attention and KV Caching With Dynamic Depth 19:55 Recurrent Depth and Chain of Thought 23:26 Recursive Self-Improvement 24:27 Universal Transformers 25:27 Latent Reasoning With Recurrent Depth 27:09 Summary
Corrections: 3:09 I incorrectly said that Nanbeige was developed in India. Nanbeige4.2-3B was developed by Nanbeige LLM Lab and Boss Zhipin in China. I had confused it with Sarvam AI, which is based in India.
If you enjoyed this video, I also write about LLM research and model architectures in my Ahead of AI newsletter: https://magazine.sebastianraschka.com/

media:group.media:title: How Claude's Text Watermarking Works
media:group.media:description:
Link to transcript: https://magazine.sebastianraschka.com/p/claude-watermarking Link to the slides: https://sebastianraschka.com/pdf/slides/2026-08-18-claude-watermarking.pdf
This video explains how Anthropic's text watermarking for Claude works. In particular, it explains how the next-token sampling process in LLMs work, and how this is modified to implement the watermarking technique. A thorough understanding of the watermarking is useful because it helps us understand the implementation shortcomings as well.

entry.title: What I Learned From Implementing LLM Architectures From Scratch (And How to Get Started)

media:group.media:title: What I Learned From Implementing LLM Architectures From Scratch (And How to Get Started)
media:group.media:description:
LLM Architecture Gallery: https://llm-gallery.com
In this talk, I discuss what we can learn from implementing LLM architectures from scratch in Python and PyTorch.
The main idea is that to really understand how modern LLMs work, it helps to inspect the actual implementation details: attention variants, normalization layers, configuration files, KV cache optimizations, and the small architectural choices that often make a model work correctly.
I also walk through how I approach new open-weight models, how I compare them against reference implementations, and what broader architecture trends emerge from looking at many recent LLMs.

entry.title: A Visual Tour of Modern LLM Architectures

media:group.media:title: A Visual Tour of Modern LLM Architectures
media:group.media:description:
LLM Architecture Gallery: https://sebastianraschka.com/llm-architecture-gallery/
In this video, I take you on a visual tour of modern LLM architectures and walk through the key ideas behind models like DeepSeek, Qwen3-Next, Kimi, Sarvam, Ling 2.5, and Nemotron.
We look at what actually changed in recent LLM design, including grouped-query attention (GQA), sliding-window attention, multi-head latent attention (MLA), DeepSeek sparse attention, and hybrid linear attention.
The goal of the gallery is to make it easier to compare architectures side by side, connect the diagrams back to papers, configs, and code, and get a clearer intuition for how today’s language models differ under the hood.
Poster: https://www.redbubble.com/i/poster/LLM-Architecture-Gallery-by-Ahead-of-AI/179274487/flk2 Articles / newsletter: https://magazine.sebastianraschka.com/p/visual-attention-variants

media:group.media:title: LLM Building Blocks & Transformer Alternatives
media:group.media:description:
Resources: - Understanding and Coding the KV Cache in LLMs from Scratch: https://magazine.sebastianraschka.com/p/coding-the-kv-cache-in-llms - The Big Architecture Comparison: https://magazine.sebastianraschka.com/p/the-big-llm-architecture-comparison - Beyond Standard LLMs: Linear Attention Hybrids, Text Diffusion, Code World Models, and Small Recursive Transformers - Reasoning From Scratch book: https://mng.bz/Nwr7
Description: Learn the core components of modern transformer-based large language models (LLMs) and the practical techniques that make inference faster and cheaper. We walk through Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), and Sliding Window Attention (SWA), show where Mixture of Experts (MoE) fits into today’s architectures, and finish with a look at promising alternatives and hybrid models beyond standard transformers.
